issues.failure_explanation:
Setting 4.4(a) prescribes $\widehat{R}_0:=\overline{r}_2(\widehat{ho}_0,
u_1,\ldots,
u_K,1)$ and $\widehat{R}_t:=\max\{\overline{r}_1(\widehat{ho}_t,t^{-(1+ eta)}),\overline{r}_2(\widehat{ho}_t,
u_1,\ldots,
u_K,(t+1)^{-2(1+ eta)})\}$ and then asserts $\CF_t$-measurability. Lemma 4.6, however, only states 'There exists $\overline{r}_1(ho,\epsilon)\in\N$ that depends on $ho,\epsilon$' (and analogously for $\overline{r}_2$): no canonical value and no Borel dependence of the thresholds on the measure $ho$ is established, unlike the explicit 'has a Borel dependence' requirement imposed on $\overline{n}$ and $\widetilde{	heta}$ in Assumption 3.5(iii). For $\overline{r}_2$ the defining property quantifies over the uncountable family $(m_k,n_k,	heta_k)$, so even the pointwise-minimal threshold is not visibly a Borel function of $ho$ without a selection argument, which the source does not supply. Hence the prescription may fail to define a random variable, and with it the $\CF_t$-measurability of $\widehat{\mu}_t=\widehat{ho}_t|_{\CX_{\widehat{R}_t}}$, the construction of the filtered space, and the conditional-expectation inequalities used in Proposition 4.5 and Theorem 4.7 are unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Replace the existence-only thresholds by the explicit, estimator- and parameter-free bounds that the proofs of Lemma 4.6 already produce (they depend on $ho$ only through $ho(\CX_r)$ and truncated second moments, and on the fixed growth constants of $
u_1,\ldots,
u_K$), defining $\overline{r}_1(ho,\epsilon)$ and $\overline{r}_2(ho,
u_1,\ldots,
u_K,\epsilon)$ as minima over $r\in\N$; these are Borel in $ho$, which restores the measurability assertion and everything downstream.
issues.overall_effect: The filtered-space construction and the adaptedness of the output process of Algorithm 1 under Setting 4.4 are not justified; consequently the conditional-expectation inequalities and the almost-sure precompactness/fixed-point conclusions of Theorem 4.7 (and of Corollary 5.3, which imports the same specification) are not established for the prescribed choice of $(\widehat{R}_t)$.
issues.title: Prescribed truncation indices in Setting 4.4 are not established to be well-defined measurable random variables
issues.why_classification: A short, local repair (replacing the existence statements by the explicit threshold maps already implicit in the proofs of Lemma 4.6) preserves every definition, theorem, rate, and advertised guarantee; no new nontrivial lemma or reorganization is needed.

issues.overall_effect: The stated error bound of Proposition 5.1(iii) is not valid over its advertised range $m\ge\underline{m}=1$; consistency with a single sample from $\mu$ is falsely asserted. No labelled downstream result is affected, since the verification of Assumption 3.5(iii) and all uses of the estimator (Setting 4.4, Corollary 5.3) only evaluate it with $m=n=\widehat{N}_{t,k}\ge\overline{n}\ge7$.
issues.title: Consistency bound of the modified entropic OT map estimator is claimed for all $m\ge\underline{m}=1$ but is unsupported below $m=2$ and false at $m=1$

Assumption 3.5(iii) requires thresholds $\overline{n}(\mu,
u,\epsilon)$ and $\widetilde{	heta}(\mu,
u,m,n,\epsilon)$ 'that ha[ve] a Borel dependence on $(\mu,
u,\epsilon)$' and on $(\mu,
u,m,n,\epsilon)$ respectively, and Setting 4.4(b) consumes this Borel dependence to declare $\widehat{N}_{t,k}$ and $\widehat{\ITheta}_{t,k}$ $\CF_t$-measurable when evaluated at the random measure $\widehat{\mu}_t$. The proof of Proposition 5.1(iii) establishes only the accuracy inequality: the constants $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4,\overline{	heta}(\mu,
u)$ are obtained by a non-constructive existence invocation of \citet{pooladian2021entropic}, $\overline{\alpha}(\mu,
u):=\min\{q+2+\alpha,4\}$ depends on the non-unique Hölder exponent $\alpha$ produced by Caffarelli regularity, and $C_{\mathrm{entr}}(\mu,
u)$ is assembled from these. No argument shows that these constants admit Borel-measurable selections in $(\mu,
u)$, nor that the displayed formulas for $\overline{n}(\mu,
u,\epsilon)$ and $\widetilde{	heta}(\mu,
u,m,n,\epsilon)$ (which depend on $\mu,
u$ only through such non-canonical constants) define Borel functions. Hence the proposition's claim that $\widehat{T}_{\mathrm{entr}}[	heta]$ satisfies Assumption 3.5(iii) is not established as stated.
